documents.title: Returns and refunds
documents.text: Unused merchandise may be returned within 30 calendar days after delivery. Warehouse inspection normally takes three business days, followed by three to seven business days for bank posting.

documents.title: Delivery status
documents.text: Standard delivery takes four to six business days. Express delivery takes one to two business days. A carrier trace is available after two business days without movement.

statuses.detail: Carrier scan unchanged for two business days

documents.title: Governed analytics metrics
documents.text: Net revenue is captured item revenue after discounts, less refunds recognized on the refund date, excluding tax and shipping. Sales bookings are not recognized revenue.

documents.title: Timezones and units
documents.text: Daily warehouse metrics use each facility's local date. Monetary records use major currency units unless the source adapter is explicitly marked otherwise.

statuses.detail: Previous local business day is complete

documents.title: RelayCache routing API
documents.text: Router.route is the current public coroutine. Router.dispatch is a deprecated compatibility alias retained through the next minor release.

documents.title: Retry ownership
documents.text: The scheduler owns attempt timing and retry.py owns pure retry-budget and delay calculations. Broker adapters own transport and acknowledgement translation.

documents.title: Latency metrics conventions
documents.text: Latency histograms must cover the slow tail: buckets end at 5.0 seconds. Emit one histogram per route with route name as a label.

documents.title: Broker acknowledgement contract
documents.text: A delivery is acknowledged exactly once, after handler completion. Adapters must not acknowledge on redelivery of an already-processed message.

documents.title: Release process
documents.text: Every closed issue that changed behavior gets a CHANGELOG entry under the upcoming version heading before the release branch is cut.

documents.title: Configuration reference
documents.text: RELAYCACHE_TIMEOUT accepts seconds as a decimal number. Values are read once at startup by config.load_settings.

# RelayCache

Route requests with `await Router.dispatch(request)`.
The scheduler owns retry timing and broker acknowledgements stay in adapters.
See `src/relaycache/router.py` for the public routing API.

from .retry import retry_delay

async def schedule_retry(job, attempt):
    delay = retry_delay(attempt)
    await job.defer(delay)
    return delay
